note: Curated long-list of Earth regions. 'tags' are expert-curated geology/process priors (1 = characteristic, 0.5 = partial) and are NOT derived from the DEM or climate data. 'category': benchmark = long-documented analog use; emerging = proposed/under-studied analog; control = negative control that should score poorly. Coordinates are approximate region centres.

tag_vocabulary.fluvial_paleo: Paleo-channels, alluvial fans, dry lake beds
tag_vocabulary.alteration: Hydrothermal, acid-saline, clay or sulfate alteration

sites.name: Atacama Desert (Yungay)
sites.heritage: Mars-like soils with extremely low organic content and a dry limit of microbial life (Navarro-Gonzalez et al., 2003, Science).
sites.limits: Air pressure ~90 kPa, versus ~0.6 kPa on Mars and none on the Moon; Earth gravity; intense coastal fog and rare rain events have no Mars equivalent.

sites.name: Puna de Atacama (Lascar-Salar)
sites.heritage: High-altitude, high-UV desert with salars and acid hydrothermal fields used as a Mars surface-chemistry and life-detection analog.
sites.limits: Volcanism here is mostly andesitic, not basaltic; pressure still ~55-60 kPa; summer rains and snow.

sites.name: Haughton Crater, Devon Island
sites.heritage: Site of the Haughton-Mars Project, a NASA-supported analog research station for exploration operations.
sites.limits: Only a ~23 km, ~39 Myr old impact structure; Earth gravity and atmosphere; 24 h summer daylight and biologically active tundra.

sites.name: McMurdo Dry Valleys (Wright Valley)
sites.heritage: Cold-desert microclimate zonation and ice-cemented soils studied as the closest Earth match to Mars mid-latitude permafrost (Marchant and Head, 2007, Icarus).
sites.limits: Atmosphere ~100x thicker than Mars; summer melt-water streams and lakes; remote logistics; strong environmental protection rules.

sites.name: Askja and Holuhraun, Iceland
sites.heritage: Basaltic highland desert used for rover and astronaut field training, including the 2014-15 Holuhraun lava field.
sites.limits: Not hyper-arid (hundreds of mm of precipitation); caldera is volcano-tectonic, not impact; seasonal snow cover.

sites.name: Mauna Kea summit region, Hawaii
sites.heritage: Palagonitic tephra from Mauna Kea (Pu'u Nene) is the source of the JSC Mars-1 simulant; PISCES and NASA RESOLVE field tests used Hawaiian basaltic terrain.
sites.limits: Basaltic Hawaiian ash is a Mars (not lunar-highland) soil analog; Earth gravity; tropical weather below the summit.

sites.name: Death Valley, California
sites.heritage: Named in the challenge brief; alluvial fans, playa evaporites and dunes are widely compared with Martian fans and basin deposits.
sites.limits: Extreme heat (not cold); atmosphere ~100 kPa; flash-flood fluvial erosion at rates far above anything on the Moon or present-day Mars.

sites.name: Craters of the Moon, Idaho
sites.heritage: Hosted the NASA BASALT biologic and operations analog program and Apollo-era astronaut field training; ice-bearing lava tubes.
sites.limits: Vegetated in places; semi-arid not hyper-arid; Earth gravity; young (<15 kyr) lava fields.

sites.name: Sunset Crater / San Francisco Volcanic Field
sites.heritage: Apollo crews trained at the nearby Cinder Lake crater field; Merriam Crater ash is the source of the JSC-1/JSC-1A lunar simulants (McKay et al., 1994).
sites.limits: Ponderosa-pine forest cover over much of the field; Earth gravity; weathered, oxidized cinders.

sites.name: Meteor (Barringer) Crater, Arizona
sites.heritage: Best-preserved small simple impact crater on Earth; Apollo astronaut geology training site.
sites.limits: A single 1.2 km crater inside a flat plateau; sedimentary target rock unlike lunar highland or basaltic Mars crust.

sites.name: Ries Crater, Germany
sites.heritage: ~24 km impact structure with suevite ejecta; Apollo 14 crew trained here.
sites.limits: Heavily eroded, agricultural and forested; temperate wet climate; poor environmental analog.

sites.name: Lanzarote (Timanfaya), Canary Islands
sites.heritage: ESA PANGAEA astronaut geology training and lava-tube research (Cueva de los Verdes); 1730-36 basaltic eruption fields.
sites.limits: Oceanic and humid-marine air mass; island coastline; Earth gravity; small tube diameters compared with lunar and Martian candidates (Sauro et al., 2020).

sites.name: Teide / Las Canadas, Tenerife
sites.heritage: Volcanic caldera and lava-tube field used by ESA and Mars/Moon simulation programs.
sites.limits: Phonolitic (evolved) rather than basaltic centre; snow cover in winter; Earth gravity.

sites.name: Mars Desert Research Station area, Utah
sites.heritage: Long-running crewed Mars-surface simulation habitat in the Morrison Formation badlands.
sites.limits: Sedimentary clay-rich badlands; terrain relief is small-scale; thermal environment is mild.

sites.name: Danakil Depression / Erta Ale
sites.heritage: Hydrothermal acid-saline pools at Dallol have been proposed as analogs for Noachian and Hesperian Mars chemistry.
sites.limits: Extreme heat; below sea level so atmospheric pressure ~101 kPa; harsh and politically sensitive field logistics.

sites.name: Dasht-e Lut (Kaluts), Iran
sites.heritage: Giant yardang field (kaluts) is a candidate for wind-erosion processes seen at Medusae Fossae and elsewhere on Mars.
sites.limits: Extreme surface heat; access and permitting constraints; no known lava tubes or ground ice.

sites.name: Qaidam Basin (Dalangtan), China
sites.heritage: High, cold, hyper-arid basin with yardangs and sulfate playas; Mars-analog base facilities exist in Qinghai.
sites.limits: Pressure ~65 kPa at 2.8-3 km altitude; salt chemistry dominated by terrestrial brines; limited English-language field data.

sites.name: Salar de Uyuni, Bolivia
sites.heritage: Vast flat salt pan at ~3.6 km altitude, a candidate for smooth-terrain landing and mobility trials and for evaporite mineralogy.
sites.limits: Extremely low relief, so it matches only the flattest Mars plains; seasonal flooding.

sites.name: Tibesti / Emi Koussi, Chad
sites.heritage: Saharan volcanic massif with the Aorounga impact structure nearby; hyper-arid with large yardang and dune fields.
sites.limits: Remote with severe access and security limits; volcanism mixes basalt and felsic rocks.

sites.name: Pinacate Volcanic Field, Mexico
sites.heritage: Basaltic maar and cinder-cone field set in the hyper-arid Sonoran Desert beside the Gran Desierto dunes.
sites.limits: Hot desert; sparse vegetation and wildlife; protected biosphere reserve.

sites.name: Wadi Rum, Jordan
sites.heritage: Hyper-arid sandstone and granite desert with dry-wadi networks and dunes; used as a Mars surface backdrop and for Mars-analog field campaigns.
sites.limits: Sedimentary and granitic bedrock (not basaltic); warm climate; no ground ice.

sites.name: Lop Nur and Lop Desert yardangs, China
sites.heritage: Dry salt-lake bed ringed by extensive yardang fields, a strong analog for wind-sculpted Martian terrain.
sites.limits: Former nuclear test region with restricted access; hot summers; low-relief terrain.

sites.name: Tolbachik lava plateau, Kamchatka
sites.heritage: Fresh basaltic scoria fields and lava tubes from the 1975-76 and 2012-13 fissure eruptions on a barren, glacier-adjacent plateau.
sites.limits: Wet maritime climate (not arid); long-distance, difficult access; seasonal snow.

sites.name: Harrat Khaybar, Saudi Arabia
sites.heritage: Hyper-arid basaltic lava field with kilometre-scale lava tubes (e.g. Umm Jirsan) that are strong analogs for subsurface shelter candidates.
sites.limits: Hot desert climate (not cold); very limited prior planetary-analog campaigns.

sites.name: Meseta de Somuncura, Patagonia
sites.heritage: Cold, windswept, sparsely vegetated basaltic plateau with scoria cones, little studied as a planetary analog.
sites.limits: Semi-arid with grass steppe; Earth gravity and atmosphere.

sites.name: Gilf Kebir plateau, Egypt
sites.heritage: Hyper-arid Saharan plateau with dune seas, wadis, and the 1.3 km Gebel Kamil impact crater.
sites.limits: Sandstone plateau (not basaltic); hot climate; remote and sensitive border region.

sites.name: Amboy Crater / Mojave lava fields
sites.heritage: Young basaltic cinder cone and lava field in hyper-arid Mojave Desert, within easy reach of NASA JPL and Johnson field teams.
sites.limits: Hot desert; small field; relatively low relief.

sites.name: Namib Sand Sea (Sossusvlei)
sites.heritage: Large linear and star dunes in one of the oldest deserts on Earth, comparable with Martian dune fields.
sites.limits: Dune-dominated, so it only informs aeolian terrain; coastal fog; quartz sand rather than basaltic sand.

sites.name: Kansas High Plains
sites.heritage: Negative control: flat agricultural plains.
sites.limits: Temperate, vegetated, with no relevant geology.

sites.name: Central Amazon lowland
sites.heritage: Negative control: dense rainforest lowland.
sites.limits: Hot, humid, vegetated; zero analog value for either body.

sites.name: Bernese Alps
sites.heritage: Negative control: glaciated high-relief alpine terrain.
sites.limits: Steep, wet, vegetated valleys; only superficially cold.

sites.name: Ganges Plain
sites.heritage: Negative control: densely farmed alluvial plain.
sites.limits: Humid, flat, populated; zero analog value.

sites.name: Nepal Himalaya
sites.heritage: Negative control: extreme-relief, monsoon-fed mountain belt.
sites.limits: Slopes far steeper than any landing or base site; monsoon climate.
